title: Pawn Endings: Both Sides Have Pawns
description: The King and Pawn ideas with pawns on both sides: winning a blocked pawn, the outside passed pawn, and holding a pawn down.
source: Every position is dealt fresh and judged by Lichess's endgame tablebase, which is perfect for seven pieces or fewer. These drills need a connection.

drills.name: Win the blocked pawn
drills.goal: One pawn each, blocking one another. Win theirs and keep yours.
drills.idea: The squares beside their pawn are the key squares. You get there by taking the opposition, and sometimes by losing a move on purpose.
method: Aim your king at the squares beside and behind their pawn. Reach one and the pawn falls.
Take the opposition on the way: make their king be the one that has to move.
If stepping straight ahead would hand them the opposition, step sideways first to lose a move.
Take the pawn only when you will still hold the opposition afterwards, so your own pawn can queen.

drills.name: The outside passed pawn
drills.goal: You have a passed pawn far from the other pawns. Use it to win.
drills.idea: The outside pawn is a decoy. Their king has to go and catch it, and while it is away your king wins the pawns on the other side.
method: Push the outside pawn to drag their king across the board.
Let them take it. It is a decoy.
While their king is busy, walk your king to their pawn on the other wing.
Win that pawn and queen yours. Count the race before you start.

drills.name: Hold a pawn down
drills.goal: You are a pawn down in a pawn ending that can still be drawn. Hold it.
drills.idea: A pawn down is not always lost. Blocking the passed pawn, taking the opposition, and swapping your pawn for the right one of theirs all save half points.
method: Keep your king in front of their passed pawn.
Take the opposition whenever their king steps up.
Keep your own pawn where their king cannot win it for free, and trade it for one of theirs when you can.
Aim for an ending you know is drawn: a rook pawn, or king in front of the pawn with the opposition.

drills.name: Random position
drills.goal: One of the drills above, and you are not told which. Work out what the position is worth first.
drills.idea: Read the position before you move: what is the material, where are the kings, and which method does it call for?
method: Name the position type before touching a piece.
